The benign explanation is coherent and most likely: the dispatch validation ran pre-commit against the working-tree queue, whose archive block could only be filled with commit_sha, parent_sha and path hashes AFTER the commit, so the validated bytes necessarily differ from the committed bytes. But the consequence stands: sources.json's parent_attested_check "both queues pass" cannot be verified from the committed record. Recorded as FINDING-09.

direction_two_artifact_facts_vs_reports.artifact_fact: run_controls.py prepared DIMACS in memory only and created no private temporary directory, whereas contracts/readiness.json temporary_files instructs "Use a private temporary directory for literal DIMACS files; embed exact bytes in transcript.json."
direction_two_artifact_facts_vs_reports.assessment: Benign and conservative — the run stopped at the resource gate before any solver launch, so no fixture file was needed, and the contract's substantive intent is satisfied because transcript.json embeds dimacs_utf8 and dimacs_sha256 for every fixture. It is disclosed inside each fixture record as input_status "literal DIMACS prepared in memory only; no temporary fixture or solver invocation", but it is not listed among report.json protocol_deviations, which is where a contract instruction not followed belongs. Recorded as FINDING-10.

direction_two_artifact_facts_vs_reports.artifact_fact: The files at .../TASK-20260905-a05748/report.json and .../TASK-20260905-b6c926/report.json are parent-authored control_plane_terminal_receipt records occupying the exact paths those tasks' claims and handoffs declared for the assigned Validator's report.
direction_two_artifact_facts_vs_reports.assessment: About as well disclosed as it can be. Each file's record_kind is control_plane_terminal_receipt, each names its author ("parent control plane"), and each states in its own body that no formal Validator report was produced or received and that no independent validation is accepted. Both release notes repeat it. The residual risk is purely one of path-based indexing: a tool or reader that checks only for the existence of a declared deliverable would see the path filled. Recorded as FINDING-11 at informational severity.

direction_two_artifact_facts_vs_reports.artifact_fact: Neither ledger/handoffs/TASK-20260905-a05748.yaml nor ledger/handoffs/TASK-20260905-b6c926.yaml carries a review_plan (both are null), though both are validator handoffs at review-adversarial / xhigh with independent_session_required true.
direction_two_artifact_facts_vs_reports.assessment: Defensible rather than a violation. AGENTS.md requires a review_plan when a handoff opens a CLAIM-CHANGING review round, and both rounds were explicitly not claim-changing: DEC-20260905-70b53c next_actions states "This administrative review authorizes no scientific claim-changing review or promotion." Recorded as FINDING-12 at informational severity, as forward guidance rather than a defect.

direction_two_artifact_facts_vs_reports.artifact_fact: Only TASK-20260905-1134be's claim did not expire (was_expired false, envelope 263 s inside a 660 s TTL). All four other producer tasks released with was_expired true.
direction_two_artifact_facts_vs_reports.assessment: An operational pattern visible only by reading the five claim/release pairs together; no report or decision mentions it. It is not evidence of a cause and this review draws no inference from it. Recorded as FINDING-13 at informational severity, since it may be useful input to the still-open question of why substantive review tasks have not delivered.

scope_discipline_check.evidence: None of the three failure records, two batch reports, or three decisions asserts a scientific conclusion. All carry scientific_conclusion null or "none". Every decision's knowledge_promotion.promoted is the empty list with an explicit not_warranted reason. hypothesis_status_changed is false and solver_readiness_pass is false in a05748. DEC-20260905-8574d7 and DEC-20260905-518d05 are both `revise`, keep the goal active, and record the review as failed with its dependent ledger stage blocked. The queues record TASK-20260905-e2c12f and TASK-20260905-86ea49 as state "blocked", matching those decisions. AGENTS.md core rule 5 — an infrastructure failure is not negative mathematical evidence — is honoured explicitly and repeatedly, including in DEC-20260905-70b53c limitations ("Infrastructure failure is not mathematical evidence") and in the readiness contract's own required_observations[4].

joints.name: delivery_acceptance_basis
joints.summary: observer.json was read first, before DEC-20260905-293536, per the review_plan's attack. Read on its own it shows a parent-side, hash-verified, timestamped observation that one spawned worker received a contract, read it, and wrote two nonce- and hash-bound files into the parent-visible worktree well inside the frozen 600-second cap. Every figure the decision quotes recomputes exactly from observer.json, and the decision's characterisation of what it shows is accurate and does not exceed it. The decision also states its own evidentiary limits correctly and explicitly denies clearing either impediment. One limitation present in the artifact's implications is absent from both records: the diagnostic's workload is not representative of the review it was diagnosing.
joints.reading_order_attestation: observer.json was opened as the first file of the entire review after the startup receipt, before DEC-20260905-293536, before BATCH-cef2eb/report.md, and before the cef2eb archive note, exactly as the review_plan's J4 attack requires. The blind statement below was fixed from observer.json alone.
blind_statement_from_observer_json_alone: A parent control plane spawned a worker task named satic_delivery_diagnostic for TASK-20260905-1134be and polled the filesystem for its two declared outputs.

The dispatch reference is 2026-09-05T18:10:45+00:00, explicitly declared conservative: it is a parent timestamp taken BEFORE the spawn call, because the exact invocation instant is not separately exposed. Using it can only overstate elapsed time, never understate it.

Poll sequence: at 18:10:45.437379 both files absent (source_head b819b430...); spawn_return at 18:11:25; at 18:11:26.024139 both still absent; at 18:12:06.794984 start.json present and report.json absent; at 18:13:14.048019 both present. Native final reply observed at 18:13:14.
Delivery bounds: start.json first observed at 81.794984 s against a 180 s early-start target; report.json at 149.048019 s against a 600 s hard cap. Both inside their bounds.

Integrity bindings all recorded as passing: both files parse; the fixed nonce delivery-cef2eb-1134be-v1 round-trips between them; report.json's start_sha256 equals the observed start.json digest; both files record the same contract_sha256 077c15af...; mandatory source hashes are recorded for AGENTS.md (42282 bytes) and agents/validator.md (8438 bytes); source head b819b430... and output-transport head be61ec27... are recorded as differing; exact byte transfer to the full worktree is recorded.
Sizes: start.json 1058 bytes, report.json 1150 bytes, each with a sha256.

What the worker itself claimed is narrow and self-limiting: claim_scope "This invocation read the start file and reproduced its nonce and SHA-256", with limitations naming that no independent evidence review was performed, that parent dispatch timing and deadline disposition are separate, and that native model memory is unmeasured. scientific_conclusion is null in start.json, in report.json, and at the top level of observer.json.
resolved_model_id is null in report.json and in the native_final_reply_observed event; model_verified is false. requested_policy review-adversarial at xhigh is recorded as REQUESTED only.
A procedure deviation is recorded: the initial contract output was truncated and the worker supplemented with read-only contract reads.

The record's own procedural_notes disclaim, unprompted, that raw first-tool output and exact aggregate input-byte telemetry are not independently exposed to the parent, that the first-tool timestamp is agent- or helper-reported, that ONE successful delivery diagnostic cannot identify the cause of the two preceding reportless review attempts, and that no independent scientific review, solver test, or resource-limit requalification was performed.

independent_recomputations.derivation: 18:12:06.794984 minus 18:10:45.000000; note the reference second is used whole, discarding the .437379 fraction, which makes the reported elapsed slightly LARGER than the true interval — conservative in the direction that disfavours the record's own conclusion

independent_recomputations.quantity: contract_sha256 recorded by both worker files

independent_recomputations.result: confirmed — delivery-cef2eb-1134be-v1 appears in both start.json and report.json
confirmed — equals this session's recomputation of start.json
both within cap, independently verified from file bytes

independent_recomputations.quantity: observer.json's own digest as quoted by the decision
opening authority commit 4a6ee87757b4... "verified over ten paths" as the decision reports
independent_recomputations.result: confirmed — the commit declares exactly 10 paths, all 10 recompute exactly at that commit, its declared parent equals its actual first parent, and it touched exactly those 10 files

comparison_with_the_decision.verdict: the decision's account of observer.json is accurate and does not exceed it
agreements: Every figure the decision's rationale quotes — 81.794984 s against the 180 s early target, 149.048019 s against the 600 s cap, the conservative 18:10:45 reference, absence at 18:10:45.437379 and 18:11:26.024139, the nonce, the start-hash binding, 1058 and 1150 bytes below 8 KiB — matches observer.json exactly and recomputes in this session.

The decision bounds its own basis correctly and unprompted: context says this Coordinator "reviewed only the supplied parent capsule ... not the underlying files or raw tool telemetry", and limitations[0] says outright "This Coordinator did not independently verify those bytes." That is an accurate statement of its evidentiary position, not a hedge.

The decision preserves the artifact's own distinction between parent observations and helper-reported timestamps: rationale[1] says the observation bounds "suffice for delivery criteria without treating helper timestamps as independently observed emission times", and limitations[1] lists the helper-reported first-tool, start-emission and finish-emission times separately as "attributed observations".

The decision carries forward every disclaimer observer.json raises: aggregate input bytes and raw first-tool transport not independently exposed, full telemetry and aggregate-read compliance not claimed, source and transport HEADs differing, resolved model null or unverified, truncated contract output and supplemental reads recorded as attributed.

The decision reproduces observer.json's most important self-limitation in substance: rationale[2] states "One successful delivery establishes no cause for prior reportless attempts and clears neither the missing independent-review impediment nor the memory/resource impediment", matching procedural_notes "One successful delivery diagnostic cannot identify the cause of the two preceding reportless review attempts."

Scope discipline holds: decision is `approve` but scoped to "the stated operational delivery criteria within this one attempt", explicitly "not an independent review of research evidence"; knowledge_promotion.promoted is empty with not_warranted "A single operational file-delivery diagnostic establishes no new scientific finding"; next_actions approves no successor execution and instructs that prior failed tasks and their blocked review-dependent gates be preserved unchanged.
divergences: None that overstates the artifact. The one gap runs the other way — a limitation the artifact's own facts imply but neither record states. See FINDING-14.

what_the_acceptance_establishes: That on one occasion in this harness a spawned worker task received a frozen contract, read it, and wrote two well-formed, nonce-bound, hash-bound JSON files into the parent-visible worktree, with parent-side polling and parent-recomputed digests as the evidence.
That the two files were first observed 81.794984 s and 149.048019 s after a conservative pre-spawn reference, hence inside the frozen 180 s early-start target and 600 s hard cap.

That the delivery-integrity bindings the contract asked for held: both files parse, the nonce round-trips, report.json binds the actual start.json digest, both record the correct contract digest, and both are within the 8 KiB output cap. All of these are independently re-verified above.
That the exact bytes reached the full worktree, since the digests recorded in the observer still recompute from the committed files today.
what_the_acceptance_does_not_establish: No cause for the two prior reportless review attempts. Both observer.json and the decision say so explicitly.
No worker-side timing. first_tool_started_at, the start emission and the finish emission are agent- or helper-reported and were never parent-observed; only file-visibility instants were.
No served-model identity. resolved_model_id is null and model_verified is false, so the record does not establish that review-adversarial at xhigh was actually served for that diagnostic.

No aggregate input-byte compliance. contracts/delivery.json sets maximum_total_input_bytes 1048576, and observer.json states the aggregate input-byte telemetry was not exposed. Separately, the contract's stop_new_work_seconds 540 appears in no parent_checks entry; it is moot here only because delivery landed at 149 s.

Nothing scientific: no independent evidence review, no solver execution, no resource requalification, no mathematical result, and no goal completion criterion. scientific_conclusion is null in every one of the three files.
Nothing about the launch-archive bindings that are the subject of J1-J3. The diagnostic did not inspect them.

That a SUBSTANTIVE review can be delivered inside the cap. The diagnostic's payload was 2208 bytes total, and by the helper's own reported timestamps the work between start emission (18:12:01.211528) and finish emission (18:12:06.872425) was 5.660897 s. That is not a representative workload for the integrity review it was diagnosing, and neither record says so. See FINDING-14.

control_outcome.contract_requirement: Apply the J1 recompute-vs-recorded method to BATCH-cef2eb, the small known-good delivery-diagnostic set, as well as to the failed batches. A method that flags everything, or flags nothing anywhere, is miscalibrated and must be reported as such.
calibration_reasoning: It does not flag nothing. The working-tree comparison raised 5 flags out of 58 bound entries, and this session's own procedure raised two further flags that had to be run down: BATCH-1a527c/archives/TASK-20260905-79a686/snapshot.md initially appeared unbound, and one transcribed excerpt initially appeared non-verbatim. Both were false positives of the reviewer's instrument rather than defects in the records, and both were resolved by widening the method — reading the second queue file, and normalising whitespace before comparing. A method that had flagged nothing anywhere would have produced none of these.

It does not flag everything. 53 of 58 working-tree comparisons matched, 58 of 58 at-commit comparisons matched, all 10 release-record digests matched, all 5 parent-reported proposal hashes matched, all 8 excerpts matched, and all 7 archive commits had correct parents and exactly-scoped diffs. The flags localised to 2 files out of the 58 bound entries.

Most importantly, the flags are UNCORRELATED with batch outcome, which is the discrimination this control exists to test. The known-good control set produced a mismatch (1 of 17) of exactly the same kind and cause as the failed sets did. So the quantity the method measures is 'a shared mutable record has moved since it was bound', not 'this batch failed'. If the working-tree flags had clustered on the failed batches and spared the control, that would have been the artifact tell — a signal that fails to vanish where its cause is absent. It did not happen.

The method also has a demonstrated discriminating mode: re-testing every flagged entry at the commit its own archive names converted all 5 working-tree flags to exact matches and, in doing so, distinguished 'binding was wrong when made' (which would have been a genuine integrity failure and was found nowhere) from 'file legitimately moved afterwards' (found in exactly 2 shared records, each with a named git-history cause).
uninformative_dimensions_reported_as_req: At-commit verification returned 58/58 exact across all three sets, so on that dimension alone the method cannot distinguish the control set from the failed sets. This is reported explicitly rather than presented as a passing grade: it means the archive-binding layer is uniformly sound across all three batches, and it means at-commit verification by itself carries no information about why two batches failed. The batches did not fail for archive-integrity reasons, so an archive-integrity check correctly finds nothing there.
The control therefore certifies the method's calibration but supplies no evidence about the delivery-failure question, which remains open and is outside this task's joints.

findings.title: The goal head carries two `impediments` lists at different nesting levels, with the id IMP-1 used twice for different impediments, and nothing validates either list.
findings.detail: The file's top-level keys are research_goal, impediments and updated_at. research_goal.impediments holds IMP-1, IMP-2 and IMP-3; a SECOND, sibling top-level `impediments` list holds another entry also called IMP-1, with entirely different content — it records that dispatch of TASK-20260905-2c383f (this task) and its dependent stage TASK-20260905-e20317 were blocked because review-adversarial at xhigh was unservable, citing DEC-20260905-e140ee. There is also a duplicated updated_at at both levels.
findings.consequence: Two distinct impediments share one identifier, so a reference to 'GOAL-SATIC-c49b77 IMP-1' is ambiguous, and the impediment describing the currently-blocked review sits outside the research_goal mapping where a consumer reading the goal record would look for it. `python3 tools/validate_ledger.py` completes with no finding against any SATIC record: grep of its full output for 'satic' and 'c49b77' returns nothing, and the string 'impediment' appears in tools/validate_ledger.py only inside remediation message text, so there is no schema check that reads either list. The defect is therefore invisible to tooling.
findings.not_a_claim_about: the science, any archive binding, or any goal status
findings.remedy_note: Records are immutable; the remedy is a superseding goal record or shard under a new identifier, authored by the Coordinator. This Validator did not modify the file.

findings.title: The goal head's `current_batch_id` and `dispatch_queue_path` still point at the first batch, four batches later.
findings.detail: At HEAD, current_batch_id is BATCH-1a527c and dispatch_queue_path is coordination/goals/GOAL-SATIC-c49b77/batches/BATCH-1a527c/dispatch_queue.json, even though the goal has since run BATCH-971dc7, BATCH-cef2eb and, per the goal's own next_action and top-level impediment, BATCH-2cca27 and BATCH-008925. The three ledger archives each rebound the goal file (verified: four distinct exact digests at four commits), so the field had four opportunities to advance and did not.
findings.consequence: A consumer that resolves the goal's active queue through dispatch_queue_path is directed to the first batch's queue, whose own review-dependent stage TASK-20260905-e2c12f is blocked. Also noted: the goal's next_action names only BATCH-2cca27's frozen contract as the single next action and does not mention BATCH-008925, while the top-level impediment does name BATCH-008925 and TASK-20260905-2c383f — so the two fields disagree about which lane is current.
findings.not_a_claim_about: the science or the validity of any batch's archives
findings.remedy_note: Coordinator's to reconcile in a superseding record. Reported, not repaired.

findings.title: Archive coverage for BATCH-1a527c is split across two queue files, and the archive notes point to 'the dispatch queue' without naming which.
findings.detail: BATCH-1a527c's launch-authority archive TASK-20260905-79a686 and its 15 bindings live in authority_queue.json, while the producer and ledger archives live in dispatch_queue.json. The 79a686 snapshot note says only that hashes 'are bound after the real commit in the dispatch queue', and the 15bed7 note similarly says bindings are 'stored in the subsequent queue receipt', neither naming a file.
findings.consequence: Purely discoverability. A reviewer scanning the conventional dispatch_queue.json alone concludes the launch-authority layer is unbound; this session made exactly that error on its first pass and corrected it only because the review_plan mandated a reverse-direction comparison. Coverage is in fact complete at 23 of 23 files for this batch, and no binding is missing.

findings.title: Per-task wall-clock budget compliance is unverifiable for three of four producer tasks, and the only available envelope for the intake exceeds its cap without attribution.
findings.detail: No worker wall-clock telemetry exists for TASK-20260905-53d333, TASK-20260905-ae8941 or TASK-20260905-b6c926. The intake states this outright (budget_measurement: 'No independent wall-clock or peak-memory telemetry collected; caps are authority fields, not measurements'), and ae8941 records it as protocol_deviations[0]; ae8941's only elapsed figure, recorder_elapsed_seconds 0.4719, times the receipt writer and not the task. The one measurable envelope for 53d333 is claim acquired_at 16:03:41Z to released_at 16:24:09Z = 1228 s against a 600 s contract cap, with was_expired true against a 900 s lease.
findings.consequence: This review establishes NEITHER compliance NOR violation of the 600-second cap. The 1228 s figure spans dispatch, claim, worker execution, release and coordinator work, and nothing in the artifacts apportions it. Stated explicitly because the coordinator prior in the review_plan expected 'unverified compliance with the 600-second cap' — this review confirms it is unverified, and adds that the one available bound is larger than the cap and cannot be attributed.
findings.not_a_claim_about: a budget violation, which is NOT asserted, and not the science
findings.note: This is an evidence gap, not misconduct. It was disclosed by the producer and by the release note before any reviewer looked.

findings.title: Two of the sources listed in sources.json carry no SHA-256 against a format clause that requires hashes.
findings.detail: contracts/design-intake.json format.sources.json requires 'Exact local source paths read, SHA-256 hashes and scope of each citation'. The two contracts_read entries — AGENTS.md and agents/idea-generator.md — both carry "sha256": null. The five proposal_sources entries do carry hashes, and this session verified all five against the actual files.
findings.consequence: Literal partial non-compliance, fully disclosed and adequately explained: the access field records that these arrived as parent-transported conversation text, so no file was opened to hash. Under AGENTS.md rule 9 the provenance marking (internal) is correct and the honest remedy is retrieval, not a repair.
findings.not_a_claim_about: fabrication — none was found anywhere in this record

findings.title: The four proof-search audits are recorded as pending without a per-audit reason field.
findings.detail: contracts/design-intake.json required_obligations[2] asks that each audit 'record pending/not-applicable with reasons'. In benchmark-obligations.json, baseline_embedding, observation_collision, quantifier_order and method_ceiling each carry status 'pending' and a 'required' string but no 'reason' key; only constructive_transforms carries an explicit reason. The reason is supplied collectively in intake.md prose ('No audit is marked not applicable because applicability has not been established from the full bodies').
findings.consequence: Minor and arguably immaterial, since the substantive prohibition — never invent a passed audit — is fully honoured and no audit is marked passed or not-applicable anywhere. Recorded for completeness against the literal obligation.

findings.title: The ranked next design action has no named `remaining_uncertainty` field.
findings.detail: contracts/design-intake.json required_obligations[3] asks for 'One ranked next design action with rationale and remaining uncertainty'. ranked_next_design_action carries rank, action, rationale, completion_gate and authority. The remaining uncertainty is present in substance — inside rationale ('The excerpt capsule does not establish sufficient semantics or dependencies to rank scientific merit') and in intake.md — but is not a distinct field.
findings.consequence: Structural only; the obligation is substantively met and exactly one action is ranked with no execution approved.

findings.title: The resource-probe outputs in the ae8941 evidence are Executor-transcribed literals, disclosed in the transcript but not in the report.
findings.detail: run_controls.py lines 58-61 define probe_outputs as two hard-coded strings and lines 63-68 emit them as the probes' stdout_utf8. The recorder never executes a probe. transcript.json discloses this per probe via capture_provenance ('Executor transcribed the exact Python source and its output from tool receipts before writing this recorder; this recorder does not rerun probes'), with start_utc, end_utc and elapsed_seconds all null and a timing_unavailable_reason. report.json discloses the missing timestamps in protocol_deviations[0] but does not disclose that the probe OUTPUTS are transcribed rather than captured; its anomalies block presents the ValueError without that qualification.
findings.consequence: This is NOT a fabrication and must not be read as one — the Executor transcribed real tool output and marked the transcription, which is compliance with AGENTS.md rule 9, and the substance is independently corroborated by the separate isolated probe embedded in BATCH-1a527c/archives/TASK-20260905-2b52a7/snapshot.md, which carries genuine returncode, stdout and elapsed_seconds and reproduces the same ValueError on all three limits. The defect is legibility: a reader of report.json alone cannot tell that its central anomaly rests on transcribed rather than captured output.
findings.not_a_claim_about: the cause of the limit failure, which every record correctly leaves undetermined, and nothing mathematical

findings.title: The transcript's authority_validation block hard-codes a success return code and embeds a plan bound to a queue state that was never committed; the plan file is not preserved.
findings.detail: run_controls.py line 105 writes authority_validation with returncode 0 and empty stdout and stderr as literals, and lines 100-101 read the plan from /tmp/satic-ae8941-authority-plan.json. That embedded plan records source_queue_sha256 df7a6c29de27f4424f219535696c45fba2b7a0ebbcf7d680a591459a3f408f4d. This session hashed authority_queue.json at every commit in its history: exactly one commit ever touched it, 4c72c94c7b78 (which is the queue_binding value sources.json records), and its content hashes to 8e74be1586a81db4d7978b907c0f281f18dad15fbd768c81421c95df1c18c518. No committed revision matches the plan's recorded hash, and the /tmp plan file is not preserved as an artifact. Unlike the resource probes, this block carries no capture_provenance field.
findings.consequence: The benign explanation is coherent and most likely correct: the validation ran pre-commit against the working-tree queue, whose archive block can only be filled with commit_sha, parent_sha and path hashes after the commit exists, so the validated bytes necessarily differ from the committed bytes. But the verifiable consequence stands — sources.json's parent_attested_checks item 'both queues pass' cannot be confirmed from the committed record, and the transcript asserts a returncode it did not capture. The archive bindings themselves are unaffected and remain exact.
findings.not_a_claim_about: fabrication, which is not asserted; nor any archive binding, all of which verify

findings.title: A contract instruction on temporary files was not followed and is not listed among the report's protocol deviations.
findings.detail: readiness.json temporary_files instructs 'Use a private temporary directory for literal DIMACS files; embed exact bytes in transcript.json.' run_controls.py created no temporary directory; each fixture records input_status 'literal DIMACS prepared in memory only; no temporary fixture or solver invocation'. The contract's substantive requirement is met — transcript.json embeds dimacs_utf8 and dimacs_sha256 for all three fixtures.
findings.consequence: Benign and arguably the more conservative choice, since the run stopped before any solver launch and no fixture file was needed. The defect is that a departure from a frozen contract instruction is disclosed only inside a per-fixture field rather than enumerated in report.json protocol_deviations, which is where AGENTS.md's procedure-deviation discipline puts it.
findings.not_a_claim_about: the fixtures, which this session independently re-enumerated and confirmed

findings.title: Parent-authored receipts occupy the exact paths declared for the assigned Validators' reports.
findings.detail: Both handoffs and both claims declare .../report.json as the validator's deliverable. Both files exist but are control_plane_terminal_receipt records authored by the parent control plane.
findings.consequence: Disclosure is thorough — each file names its record_kind and author and states in its own body that no formal Validator report was produced or received and that no independent validation is accepted; both release notes repeat it; both decisions repeat it. The only residual risk is to a tool or reader that tests for the existence of a declared deliverable rather than its authorship. Recorded as informational because the records themselves close the gap.
findings.not_a_claim_about: anything; the absence of those two reports is already the recorded state and IMP-1 already tracks it

findings.title: The two failed validator handoffs carry no review_plan.
findings.detail: Both are validator handoffs at review-adversarial / xhigh with independent_session_required true and review_plan null.
findings.consequence: Defensible, not a violation. AGENTS.md requires a review_plan when a handoff opens a CLAIM-CHANGING review round, and DEC-20260905-70b53c states explicitly that 'This administrative review authorizes no scientific claim-changing review or promotion.' Recorded as forward guidance: a round that could move a hypothesis status, close a lane, or support a headline claim needs a plan written before any reviewer runs. This task's own handoff does carry one.

findings.title: Only the successful delivery diagnostic released without an expired claim; the other four producer tasks all did.
findings.detail: Claim-to-release envelopes against lease TTLs: 53d333 1228 s / 900 s expired; a05748 1495 s / 720 s expired; ae8941 787 s / 600 s expired; b6c926 377 s / 300 s expired; 1134be 263 s / 660 s NOT expired. Recorded in no report or decision.
findings.consequence: An operational pattern visible only by reading the five claim/release pairs together. This review draws NO causal inference from it — an expired lease is not evidence of anything mathematical, and correlation across five records is not a cause. Surfaced because the still-open question of why substantive review tasks have not delivered is being worked, and this is a cheap, already-recorded datum for whoever works it.
findings.not_a_claim_about: the cause of any failure, and nothing scientific

findings.title: Neither observer.json nor the accepting decision states that the delivery diagnostic's workload is unrepresentative of the review it was diagnosing.
findings.detail: The diagnostic's total payload was 2208 bytes (1058 + 1150), and by the helper's own reported timestamps the interval from start emission 18:12:01.211528 to finish emission 18:12:06.872425 was 5.660897 s. Both records state clearly that one success 'diagnoses no cause of earlier failures', but neither states the distinct point that a 2 KB, ~6-second write is not a proxy for a substantive multi-joint integrity review, so 'delivery works' transfers to a real review workload only under an unstated assumption.
findings.consequence: Cause and transferability are separate limitations, and only the first is recorded. The gap matters because the diagnostic was authorized precisely to unblock a substantive review, and the goal's own top-level impediment shows that review still did not proceed on the next attempt. Recorded as a limitation missing from the records, not as a defect in the diagnostic, which did exactly what its frozen contract asked.
